title: How to insert an icon in PowerPoint on Mac: step by step for Microsoft 365
metaTitle: How to Insert an Icon in PowerPoint on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to insert an icon in PowerPoint on Mac with Insert > Icons, then recolor it, fix a missing menu, and check your Office version.
targetKeyword: how to insert an icon in powerpoint on mac
intro: To insert an icon in PowerPoint on Mac, open the Insert menu, choose Icons, pick the one you want, and click Insert in the lower right. Select several icons before you click Insert to add them all at once, then recolor them with Format Graphic > Fill > Solid fill.
tldr: Go to Insert > Icons in PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 on your Mac.
Search by keyword, scroll, or pick a category in the navigation pane.
Choose each icon you want, then click Insert in the lower right.
To recolor, right-click the icon and choose Format Graphic > Fill > Solid fill.
If Icons is missing, update macOS and Office, then check the menu again.

blocks.text: Icons give a slide a quick visual cue. A checkmark can mark a finished step, and a warning sign can flag a risk. PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 on Mac has a built-in icon library, so you don't need to download files first. This guide covers the Mac desktop app. The browser version has a similar menu, and the differences are covered further down.
What you need before you start

You need PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, signed in with your account. Microsoft's stock images article says full library access requires a Microsoft 365 subscription and sign-in. Office 2021 and Office for the web users who don't subscribe get only a portion of the library. If you see fewer icons than a colleague sees, check your sign-in status first.

items: Microsoft 365 for Mac, signed in, for the full icon library.
macOS 12 Monterey or later if you plan to update Office from inside the app.
An internet connection, because icons load from Microsoft's online stock library.
A deck open in Normal view, with the slide you want to change selected.

blocks.text: Insert an icon in PowerPoint on Mac, step by step

The numbered steps sit in the steps section of this page. Follow them once, in order, and the menu will feel familiar after your first slide. The menu bar sits at the top of your screen, so the Insert menu lives there, not inside the PowerPoint window. Icons land on the slide you have selected, so check the thumbnail before you start.
Search and browse the icon library

The icon panel gives you three ways to find something. You can scroll the whole set, type a keyword in the search box, or click a category in the navigation pane. Search is faster when you know the word. Try plain nouns such as 'arrow', 'phone', or 'chart' before you try an abstract idea. If a word returns nothing, try a synonym. Scrolling helps when you aren't sure what you want and need to see the options.
Insert several icons in one go

Microsoft says you can select several icons before you click Insert. Click the first icon, click the next, and keep going until your set is chosen. Then click Insert once in the lower right, and all of them land on the current slide. This saves trips back to the menu when you build a row of status symbols or a simple process diagram. Pick the wrong one? Nothing is added until you click Insert, so you can still change the selection.
Recolor an icon to match your deck

Right-click the icon on the slide and choose Format Graphic. Under Fill, select Solid fill, then pick a color. The whole icon changes at once. Choose a color from your theme so the icon matches your headings and charts. Recoloring happens on the slide, not in the icon panel, so insert the icon first.
Quick reference for icon tasks

rows: Choose it, then click Insert in the lower right.

blocks.text: Why an icon takes only one color on a Mac

Microsoft's SVG article says that on Mac, Fill applies one color to the whole image. To color parts of an icon differently, you have to convert it to a shape. Microsoft says that route currently needs Office for Microsoft 365 on Windows. The article doesn't say the part-by-part route works on a Mac. Plan on one color per icon unless you have a Windows machine handy.

blocks.title: Test before you promise
blocks.text: Don't promise a multi-color icon to a client until you have tested it on your own Mac. Microsoft's SVG article doesn't give a Mac route for it.
Two paths to the icon library

Microsoft documents two ways in. The first is Insert > Icons, which this guide follows. The second is Insert > Pictures > Stock Images, and Microsoft's support page places the Icons collection under it. If the first path won't open for you, try the second one.
When the Icons option is missing in PowerPoint on Mac

A 2018 Microsoft Q&A thread describes a subscriber whose Insert Icon option disappeared. A Microsoft representative had said Office 2016 for Mac version 16.14.1 includes the feature. The fix an MVP suggested was to update macOS through the App Store first. Then open Help > Check for Updates in any Office app and let AutoUpdate install updates. Restart the Mac when it finishes. That thread uses the older product names, so your menus may look a little different.
Check your Office version and update it

Open any Office app and choose Help > Check for Updates. If Microsoft AutoUpdate opens, click Update or Update All, then restart the app when it finishes. Microsoft says macOS 12 Monterey or later is required for this update path. The newest Office for Mac release in Microsoft's notes is 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026.
Those release notes don't mention Insert > Icons. A new version number won't tell you whether the icon library changed, so test your own menu after each update.
Icons that won't load or insert

Stock content can fail for reasons outside your Mac. On August 15, 2022, an expired certificate for Microsoft's stock images server made about half the stock content unavailable, icons included. Inserting an item gave an error. Office Watch suggested a quick check: go to Insert > Pictures > Stock Images and see whether content loads.
If the library won't load, check your internet connection and sign-in first. Then try again later. If it still fails, the problem may be on Microsoft's side, not in your Mac settings.
How the web version differs

Microsoft's Insert icons article says Insert > Icons works only in PowerPoint among the Microsoft 365 web apps. The steps match the Mac app. Go to Insert > Icons, search or scroll, then click Insert at the lower right. Browser menus can differ in labels and placement, so match the names you see rather than the layout in this guide.
Keyboard shortcuts and the mouse

Microsoft's icon article lists no keyboard shortcut for icons. Its newer Mac shortcut list doesn't include Insert > Icons either. Use the menu for that step. Related shortcuts still help once the icon is on the slide. Control-click opens the context menu for the selected object, according to Indezine. Paste formatting is ⇧⌘V, which copies the look of one object onto another.
Mistakes people make with icons

The most common slip is closing the panel after you click an icon. Clicking an icon only selects it. You must click Insert in the lower right to add it to the slide. The second slip is looking for a color option in the icon panel. Recolor on the slide, after the icon lands.

The third slip is expecting a multi-color icon to recolor part by part. On Mac, the documented route colors the whole icon. Set that expectation before you start a large deck, and pick colors that work in one tone.
Who uses icons in PowerPoint

Consultants and instructional designers build many decks from templates. Icons help them label steps, flag risks, and mark progress without extra text. If your team keeps a master slide, add the icons there so every slide gets the same style. See [how to edit the slide master in PowerPoint](/how-to/edit-the-slide-master-in-powerpoint). For role-specific tips, read [PowerPoint for consultants on Mac](/for/consultants/powerpoint).
Next steps after your icons are in

Once the icons sit where you want them, check the deck from the audience side. Run [Presenter View](/how-to/use-presenter-view-in-powerpoint) on a second screen so your notes and the slide show side by side. If you plan to share the deck as a video, [save as a video](/how-to/save-as-a-video-in-powerpoint) after the icons are final.

If you're new to icons, start with one slide. Insert a single icon, recolor it, and move it into place. Then repeat the pattern on the next slide. Once the steps feel natural, the menu stops being the slow part of the job.

faq.question: Why don't I see Insert > Icons in PowerPoint for Mac?
faq.answer: Check that you use PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 or a build that includes the feature. A 2018 Microsoft Q&A says Office 2016 for Mac version 16.14.1 included Insert > Icons. If it's still missing, update macOS, then run Help > Check for Updates.

faq.question: Can I insert icons without a Microsoft 365 subscription?
faq.answer: You can reach the library, but only part of it. Microsoft's stock images article says full library access needs a Microsoft 365 subscription and sign-in. Office 2021 and Office for the web users who don't subscribe get only a portion of the library.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to insert an icon?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft's icon article lists none, and its newer Mac shortcut list doesn't include Insert > Icons. Use the menu for that step. Control-click opens the context menu for an icon after it's on the slide.

faq.question: Can I change the color of just one part of an icon on Mac?
faq.answer: Not with the documented steps. Format Graphic > Fill applies one color to the whole icon on Mac. Microsoft's SVG article says converting to a shape for part-by-part color currently needs Office for Microsoft 365 on Windows.

faq.question: Why do my icons show an error or fail to load?
faq.answer: Stock content can fail on Microsoft's side. On August 15, 2022, an expired certificate made about half the stock content unavailable, including icons. Check Insert > Pictures > Stock Images to see whether content loads, then try again later.

faq.question: Do I insert icons the same way in PowerPoint for the web?
faq.answer: The steps are similar. Microsoft says Insert > Icons works only in PowerPoint among the Microsoft 365 web apps. Look for Insert > Icons, search or scroll, then click Insert at the lower right.

faq.question: Will an Office update change how icons work?
faq.answer: It might. Microsoft's Office for Mac release notes don't mention Insert > Icons in the latest entries. The newest release listed is 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. Check the notes if icons behave differently after an update.

steps.name: Open the slide
steps.text: In Normal view, click the slide thumbnail where the icon belongs. The icon goes onto the slide that is selected, so make sure the right one is highlighted before you start. For a new slide, add it first from the New Slide button on the Home tab.

steps.name: Open the Insert menu
steps.text: Click Insert in the menu bar at the top of your screen. The menu bar stays at the top of the display, not inside the PowerPoint window.

steps.name: Choose Icons
steps.text: Click Icons in the Insert menu. A panel opens with the icon library and a navigation pane for categories.
steps.tip: If Icons isn't in the menu, see the troubleshooting list below.

steps.name: Find your icon
steps.text: Scroll the library, type a keyword in the search box, or pick a category in the navigation pane. Search is the quickest route when you know the word you want.

steps.name: Select one or more icons
steps.text: Click an icon to choose it. To insert several, choose each one before you click Insert. Nothing is added to the slide until you click Insert.

steps.name: Click Insert
steps.text: Click Insert in the lower right of the panel. The selected icon or icons appear on the current slide, and you can drag them into place.
steps.tip: Keep the right slide selected so the icons land where you expect.

steps.name: Recolor the icon
steps.text: Right-click the icon on the slide, then choose Format Graphic. Under Fill, select Solid fill and pick a color. The whole icon changes to that color.
steps.tip: On a trackpad, use two fingers or Control-click to open the same menu.

steps.name: Resize and place
steps.text: Drag a corner handle to resize the icon, and drag the icon itself to move it. Repeat the steps for any other icon you need on the slide.

troubleshooting.problem: Insert > Icons is missing from the Insert menu
troubleshooting.fix: Update macOS through the App Store first. Then open Help > Check for Updates in any Office app, click Update or Update All in AutoUpdate, and restart the Mac. A 2018 Microsoft Q&A thread describes this fix.

troubleshooting.problem: The icon panel is empty or shows an error
troubleshooting.fix: Check your internet connection and sign-in. Then open Insert > Pictures > Stock Images to see whether content loads there. A certificate outage on August 15, 2022 hit stock content, so wait and try later if the whole library fails.

troubleshooting.problem: Icons won't recolor part by part
troubleshooting.fix: On Mac, Fill applies one color to the whole icon. Microsoft says converting to a shape for part-by-part color currently needs Office for Microsoft 365 on Windows. Use one color, or do the part-by-part work on a Windows machine.

troubleshooting.problem: Clicking an icon doesn't add it to the slide
troubleshooting.fix: Selecting an icon only chooses it. Click Insert in the lower right of the panel to add it to the current slide.

troubleshooting.problem: The Insert menu isn't where this guide says
troubleshooting.fix: Check the menu bar at the top of your screen. Labels can differ between the Mac app and the web app, and between versions. Match the names you see, then run Help > Check for Updates.
